0. 0.1 This

FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 December 1983, after the draft finalized by the Sports Goods Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council. 0.2 The requirements for cricket and hockey balls were earlier covered At the time of revision, the Committee responsible in IS : 416-1978*. for preparing this standard had decided to separate the requirements Consequently, the revised for cricket and hockey balls in two standards. requirements for hockey balls only were covered in IS : 416-19837.

0.2.1 In this standard requirements for three grades of cricket balls have been covered in place of two grades covered in earlier standards. Besides, some tests have also been covered to evaluate performance of cricket balls.
0.3 While preparing this standard assistance BS 5993 : 1980 `Specification for leather-covered the British Standards Institution. has been derived from cricket balls', issued by

NOTE 1 - The lower the number of the grade the more tightly specified are the criteria that determine the performance of the cricket balls. Grades I and 2 cricket balls are not considered satisfactory for use in first class cricket matches. NOTE 2 - The words men's, women's and junior are to signify that the dimensions and mass of the cricket balls are within the limits required by the laws of games in relation respecfively to men's, women's and junior cricket matches.

3. MATERIALS

- The core for special grade shall be made from corkwood and new wool ( 3-4 ply ), the yarn being 89 tex ( 10s count ) worsted. The proportion by mass of cork and wool shall be 2 : 1 ( f 5 percent ).
3.1.1 The core for Grades 1 and 2 shall be made from corkwood and new wool ( 3-4 ply ), the yarn being 89 tex ( 10s count ) worsted. The proportion by mass of cork and wool shall be 5 : 4 ( * 5 percent ) along with ready made centre of cork weighing 28 f 3 g. 3.2 Cover The material for cover shall conform to IS : 4553-1983*.

4.3 Height of Seam and of External Stitching - The height of the seam and of external stitching of special grade of cricket balls, when measured in accordance with the method described in 12.4, shall be between 0.5 to 0.9 mm.
NOTE - The height of seam and balls are not specified. of external stitching of Grades 1 and 2 cricket

5. REQUIREMENTS 5.1 General - Each cricket ball shall comprise a cover made from four pieces of leather stitched together around a core in such a way that the two closing or quarter seams shall be positioned diametrically opposite each other. 5.2 Covers Each half 5.2.1 The covers of all grades shall be made in two halves. shall comprise two pieces of leather joined together by a closing or The seam shall be sewn with quarter seam which is stitched internally. a waxed hemp thread of 1.5 mmnominal diameter and there shall be not less than 18 stitches. 5.3 Internal Stitching 5.3.1 The thread used for inner stitching shall be flax/cotton or equivalent quality of thread having a minimum breaking strength of The thread for mouth and outer seam stitching shall 168 N ( 16.8 kgf ). have minimum breaking strength of 100 N ( 10 kgf ) for special grade and 60 N ( 6 kgf) for Grades 1 and 2. 5.4 External Stitching

5.4.1 S'ccial Grade - The two halves of the cover shall be joined together around a core by three double rows of double stitching, the ~stitching being carried out in such a way that each of the rows The two outer double rows contributes to the strength of the seam. shall be stitched with a thread of 1 mm nominal diameter linen flax/ cotton. There shall be not less than 80 stitches and not more than 85 stitches in each row ( see Fig. 1 ). 5

IS : 10800- 1983

SAMPLE OF DOUBLE STITCHING OF ROWS 3 AND I'.

Fro.

1

STITCHING

5.4.2 Grade I - The two halves of the cover shall be joined together around a core by three double rows of double stitching, the stitching being carried out in such a way that each of the rows contributes to the The two outer double rows shall be stitched with strength of the seam. a thread of 0.7 mm to 1 mm nominal diameter linen flax/cotton. There shall be not less than 75 stitches in each row ( see Fig. 1 ).

5.4.3 Grade Z - The two halves of the cover shall be joined together around a core by one double row of double stitching, the stitching being carried out in such a way that the row contributes to the strength of the seam. ln addition, there shall be four outer single rows of double stitching. The stitching shall be with a thread of 07 mm nominal diameter. There shall be not less than 65 stitches in each row ( see Fig. 1). 5.5 Finish 5.5.1 The finished a shine. 5.6 Colour 5.6.1 The colour of the cover of the cricket ball shall be red, the shade being agreed between manufacturer and purchaser. 5.6.2 The external stitching shall be white or natural. 6. IS : 10800- 1983 11. PACKING 11.1 The balls shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper, and packed in cardboard boxes in accordance with the best prevalent trade practice. 12. METHODS OF TEST

12.1 Atmosphere for Tests - The tests shall be carried out in an atmosphere of temperature 27�C 2 2�C and relative humidity -65 f 5 percent. 12.2 Measurement of Circumference - The test shall be carried out using circumference gauges of the form shown in Fig. 2, with circumferences as stated in Table 1.

FIG. 2

CIRCUMFERENCE GAUGE

12.2.1 The cricket ball shall be placed with its seem perpendicular to the plane of the appropriate minimum circumference gauge. The cricket ball shall be rotated through 360", keeping the seam perpendicular to the plane of the gauge. The cricket ball shall not pass through the gauge, in any position. 10

IS:10800 12.2.2 The test shall be repeated circumference gauge. The cricket gauge, in any position. using the ball shall

12.3 Measurement of Seam Width - The width shall be measured across the outer edges of the seam ( see Fig. 3 ), at six positions around the seam. The positions shall be selected so as to measure the maximum and minimum widths and the four other positions shall be at each 90" increments of the circumference of the ball.

FIG.

3

WIDTH ACROSSOUTER EDGES OF SEAM

12.3.1 From the six results, the mean width of the seam and the deviation from the mean of the maximum and minimum widths shall be calcuiated. 12.4 Measurement of the Height External Stitching - A magnification shall be projected on to a screen. of the Seam and of 10 x the profile of of the the ball

12.4.1 Using the magnified profile, the projected height of the stitching and of the seam from a line drawn tangentially to the surface of the ball ( see Fig. 4 ) at four positions positioned equally spaced around the From the maximum and minimum results se-am shall be measured. obtained, the actual maximum and minimum heights of the seam and of the external stitching shall be calculated. 11

IS : 10800 - 1983 12.6 Measurement of Height of Bounce - The cricket ball shall be allowed to fall freely through a distance of 2 m on to a smooth, flat The height of the first bounce shall be horizontal concrete base. measured from the bottom of the ball. 12.6.1 The test shall be repeated in order to obtain ten valid results, The mean value ( bounces on the seam of the ball are to be ignored ). of the five highest valid results shall be calculated to the nearest 10 mm. 12.7 Measurement of Hardness and Impact Resistance a steel

12.7.1 The apparatus shall consist of a flat steel base plate, guided striker, release mechanism land suitable instrumentation.

12.7.1.1 The base plate shall be attached to a rigid monolithic base of concrete having a mass of at least 1000 kg and height of at least 0'9 m. The striker shall have mass of 5 kg f 0.1 kg, with a flat The striker shall be able circular striking surface of diameter 125 mm. to drop through a distance of at least 2 m in a guided fall with minimum retardation from the guides. The guide shall be vertical to within 1 in 400. 12.7.1.2 Attached firmly to the -striker shall be an acceleration transducer with its sensitive axis coincident to that of the striker within shall be capable of withstanding a 200 g shock f 2". The transducer without damage. 12.7.2 Measurement of Hardness - The cricket ball shall be placed with The striker shall be raised to a its seam parallel to the base plate. a height of 1.1 m above the surface of the cricket ball. The striker shall be released and the peak deceleration (g) during impact shall be measured. This value shall be recorded as the hardness of the cricket ball. 12.7.3 Impact Test - The impact test shall be carried out by using the apparatus described in 12.7.1 and the method described in 12.7.2 except that (a) the striker is raised to a height of 2-O m above the surface of the cricket ball and (b) the peak deceleration need not be recorded.

A

AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY FOR CRICKET BALLS

A-l.1 In any consignment, all the balls of the same grade, designation and manufactured from the same raw material under similar conditions shall be grouped together to constitute a lo-t. A-l.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of the standard, samples of ball shall be selected and tested separately from each lot. A-2. SAMPLING

A-2.1 The number of balls to be selected at random from the lot shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in accordance with co1 1, 2 and 5 of Table 8. 15
